messages.author: 3b5b69b5e7c80915
messages.subject: Is there a voting page for requesting a new function?
parts:
Hi,

Is there a voting page for requesting a new function?  It will be useful information for developers' prioritization.

I believe that many of the users want stan to have more usability and scalability, that is to say, discrete parameter and multi-threading, even if developers are not champions about them. For example, Supervised LDA and Relation Topic Model use the realized category indexes z instead of theta (topic distribution). Summing out doesn't work, right?
http://people.ee.duke.edu/~lcarin/Iulian6.6.08.pdf

Regards,
Bero

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is there a voting page for requesting a new function?
parts:
On May 13, 2014, at 11:57 PM, Bero <heart...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> Is there a voting page for requesting a new function? It will be useful information for developers' prioritization.

Not as such. Feel free to comment here --- the developers
read these posts, or on the issue tracker, which is where
we keep track of feature requests. Bigger things we keep design
docs on in the Wiki.

>
> I believe that many of the users want stan to have more usability and scalability,
Absolutely! But then you have to say for which kinds of models.
> that is to say, discrete parameter and multi-threading, even if developers are not champions about them.

I think I can speak for all the developers in saying we are not
at all opposed to discrete parameters or multi-threaded evaluation,
it's just that we don't know how to implement them. Having said that,
it's also not where we're putting our efforts, but I think that's
largely because we don't know how to. Similarly, we've had requests
for map-reduce type implementations and for GPU-type implementations,
as well as multi-threaded implementations (for those not up on the various
ways to parallelize these days: GPUs parallelize shared ops across
graphics processors, map-reduce more general operations across core processes --- usually across
machines on a cluster, and multi-threaded implementations use multiple
cores on a single machine).

For discrete parameters, we can't just calculate the Markov blanket
use conditional sampling --- Stan's language doesn't define a graphical
model the same way a BUGS or JAGS model does. We're very open to
suggestions on how we might do sampling. We could take a very brute-force
approach and use the entire joint density/mass function and Bayes's law,
but it'd be very slow.

As to multi-threading, it'd be easy to do with a matrix library
that multi-threaded if you reimplemented all of Stan's underlying
data types, code generation, etc. Or if Eigen, which is what we use
now, supported multi-threaded matrix evals. At a higher level, we
don't know how to deal with multi-threaded evaluation in the face of
the need for automatic differentiation.

One place we might be able to multi-thread is with higher-order derivatives
like Hessians and with multivariate first-order Jacobians (though we rarely have to
explicitly compute Jacobians by auto-diff --- the place we will need to do it
is in stiff diff eq solving).

Our priorities for the immediate future are functions (due out in next
release), differential equation solvers (probably the release after that),
more efficient auto-diff and data types for higher-order models (coming in pieces,
starting in the next release). We're also refactoring all of our interfaces
deeper into C++ to make it easier to support command-line, R and Python.
On the nearer, but not immediate term, we're going to introduce lots of point
estimation including EP, VB, and maximal marginal likelihood. The plan is
to include data parallelization for EP and stochastic VB.

So it's not lack of interest --- we just have our hands full. If people want
to volunteer, we're always looking for developers. Especially if you can
figure out how to multi-threading and discrete sampling!
> For example, Supervised LDA and Relation Topic Model use the realized category indexes z instead of theta (topic distribution). Summing out doesn't work, right?

I'm pretty sure you could sum things out for supervised LDA of various
kinds, including that described by Blei and McAuliffe in the linked doc.

> http://people.ee.duke.edu/~lcarin/Iulian6.6.08.pdf

Observed categorical outputs are no problem.

I've built similar models for crowdsourcing (following Raykar et al.'s
JMLR paper) and for population models (following the CJS model with
predictors --- I didn't actually build this one, a user did). In both
cases you get a mixed of observed and latent discrete parameters, the
latent ones of which can be marginalized out.

Not to say it's easy. We'd much rather have the marginalization be
automatic and also to support explicit discrete parameters.

I don't know the relation topic model.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is there a voting page for requesting a new function?
parts:
I'm sorry for frequent requests. I'm very happy to hear it's not lack of interest and just there is no good way to implement them for now. 

I want to ask how to marginalize out the latent variables in supervised LDA, I will make another thread.

Many thanks,
Be
